chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Defending rock guitar and its blues roots
summary: Collins says rock is hard to play, is an offshoot of the blues, and is a challenge he enjoys.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Would you say a lot now? (Inaudible).

Well, actually it's -- a lot of people put it down but it's not easy to play, especially rock guitarist have to be tremendous technicians. You know, it's a lot to be said for rock. I can't put it down. Because I enjoy it. I think I enjoy anything that's well played. You know. So I -- sure, I enjoy playing rock. I would prefer playing, you know, jazz, you know, because I'm a jazz oriented musician. But I'm also --
Can't a good jazz musician almost always play rock?
I think the question I was asking was, And he has the ability to play rock if he's willing?
Yes, I imagine so, but quite a few jazz musicians refuse to play rock. But for me it's a challenge, you know.

I just think that I can do it. I've always thought that I can do it and it's nothing -- it's music. You know, it's music, I have the technique, and it's blues oriented. That's really where it comes from and those are my roots, you know. Blues, I am -- I am blues oriented. You wouldn't think so but I came up in the south, and I heard blues guitarists all of my life, and you know, I can really appreciate the blues. The real blues, you know. And I can play the blues, you know.
So rock is an offshoot of blues, so it's, you know.
